extracted.intended_audience: mathematical problem solvers / inequality researchers / olympiad-style contestants
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of inequality problems with proposed solutions illustrating standard proof techniques (homogenization, Jensen, Cauchy, AM-GM, tangent-line method, triangle identities). The page is aimed at constructing or verifying rigorous inequality proofs in contest/journal style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogenization / normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: When the inequality is homogeneous, assume a convenient normalization (e.g., x+y+z = constant or product = 1) WLOG to reduce variables and simplify the inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly: e.g., 'Since the inequality is homogenious, we could suppose WLOG that a+b+c = 1 (or other constant) and reduce the inequality accordingly.' Guidance: apply substitution to remove scale, then prove the normalized inequality. Note equality cases should be checked under the normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show convexity and apply Jensen's inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Define an appropriate one-variable function f(t) whose sum appears in the inequality, show f''(t) > 0 (convexity), and apply Jensen to bound the sum by f(average).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in text: define f(x)=... compute f''(x)>0 so f is convex, then ∑ f(x_i) ≥ n f(average). Useful when terms are of form g(x)/(h(x)) or symmetric expressions; verify domain and differentiability and compute second derivative explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AM ≥ GM (Arithmetic Mean ≥ Geometric Mean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the AM≥GM inequality to compare sums and products and derive lower/upper bounds in various manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses 'MA≥MG' and variants multiple times to obtain simple bounds and to convert sums to products (or vice versa). Use this when you can express target terms as arithmetic means of nonnegative quantities or to deduce simple inequalities like x+y+z ≥ 3√[3]{xyz}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality (including weighted/ponderada forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Cauchy (Cauchy–Schwarz) inequality to bound sums/products, often in the form (∑ u_i^2)(∑ v_i^2) ≥ (∑ u_i v_i)^2, or its weighted variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several solutions invoke 'desigualdad de Cauchy' and a weighted Cauchy form to transform sums of rational expressions or to derive product-sum bounds. Typical pattern: apply Cauchy to group denominators or to deduce (∑ A_i/B_i)⋅(∑ A_i B_i) ≥ (∑ A_i)^2. Check applicability and nonnegativity assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chebyshev inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Chebyshev's inequality to relate the sum of products to the product of sums when sequences are similarly sorted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as the justification for a final comparison step in one solution ('the last step come from Chebyshev’s inequality'). Apply when sequences have the same monotonicity to bound averages of products by product of averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent-line (Tangent) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a tangent line to a convex (or concave) function at a chosen point and use that line as a linear lower (or upper) bound to prove the inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: define f(x)=..., compute tangent at a point and show f(x) ≥ tangent_line(x) (or ≤), then sum such inequalities to obtain the desired bound. Useful for inequalities where Jensen is hard to apply directly or when seeking sharp linear bounds leading to equality at specific points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-mean / m-th power theorem (power mean techniques)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the m-th power (power mean) inequalities/theorems to compare sums of powers and derive inequalities between symmetric sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as 'm-th power theorem' in derivations to move from sums of powers to products or other symmetric expressions. Use when dealing with ∑ x^m or when raising both sides to a power simplifies comparison; watch monotonicity of power means and sign constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution / change of variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce new variables (e.g., set a=(u+v), or relate triangle elements to s,R,r, or set normalized variables) to transform the inequality into a more tractable or standard form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include substitutions relating triangle side expressions to inradius/circumradius or setting normalized variables so that sums/products equal 1. Guidance: choose substitutions that exploit symmetry or known identities so classical inequalities become applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use known triangle identities and classical inequalities (Gerretsen, relations for incenter/inradius/circumradius)
rubrics_metrics.description: In triangle-related problems, use standard identities expressing distances (e.g., distances from incenter to vertices), relations among s,R,r (semiperimeter, circumradius, inradius), and Gerretsen-type inequalities to bound symmetric sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists identities like expressions for (I A), (I B), (I C) in terms of sides and semiperimeter and invokes Gerretsen inequality connecting R, r, s. Use these to reduce geometric sums to algebraic symmetric sums; remember domain restrictions and equality cases (often for equilateral triangle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and state equality cases explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and state when equality holds (usually when variables are equal or at particular symmetric configurations) to verify sharpness of the inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple solutions conclude 'Equality: a=b=c' or similar. After normalizing, test constant or symmetric assignments as likely extremal cases. Stating equality conditions helps verify correctness and indicates whether bounds are sharp.

rubrics_metrics.name: AM–HM and AM–GM comparisons as auxiliary steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply inequalities like AM ≥ HM or AM ≥ GM as intermediate tools to compare sums, harmonic means, and other aggregated quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside other classical inequalities to derive intermediate bounds (e.g., converting sum bounds to product bounds). Ensure denominators are positive and apply the correct mean inequality for the context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic rearrangement and factorization strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform sum/product expansions, grouping, and factorization to rewrite the inequality into forms suitable for applying classical inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the solutions, lengthy algebraic manipulations are used to transform expressions into sums of symmetric terms or products amenable to AM-GM/Cauchy. Guidance: keep track of symmetric structure and look for common factors or symmetric sums like ∑ ab, ∑ a^2, abc to leverage known inequalities.
